carousels.hook: ChatGPT’s free plan trains on your pasted customer data
carousels.throughline: ChatGPT’s free plan uses your pasted data to train its model—here’s how to opt out and keep customer details private.

reel_beats.hook: You’re training ChatGPT on your customer list for free

body.text: ChatGPT’s free plan uses every paste to improve its answers, including customer data.
Names, emails, or notes could end up in future responses to other users.
Open Settings → Data Controls → turn off ‘Improve the model for everyone.’
This one toggle stops OpenAI from using your pastes to train future models.

carousels.hook: Gmail ignores ‘free’ if your list replies
carousels.throughline: Gmail’s spam filter prioritizes sender trust over subject line keywords—using ‘free’ won’t hurt deliverability if your list engages.

reel_beats.hook: Gmail ignores ‘free’ if your list replies

body.text: Gmail’s spam filter checks sender reputation first, not the words in your subject line.
If your list replies, Gmail sees you as a trusted sender—even if you use ‘free.’
Spam filters flag ignored emails, not ones with certain words.
Focus on getting replies, not avoiding words—Gmail rewards engagement over tricks.

body.text: Google Ads labels clicks as ‘low intent’ based on search history, not actual purchases.
The Search Terms report shows which searches led to sales—even if Google called them cold.
Sort by conversions to find ‘low intent’ searches that actually bought.
Add these terms as exact match keywords to stop wasting budget on wrong labels.

carousels.caption: Meta Ads freeze if no one buys for 2 days—here’s how to restart learning without losing data or doubling spend. #metaadstips #paidsocialtips #leadgeneration #dublinbusiness
carousels.hook: Meta Ads freeze if no one buys for 2 days
carousels.throughline: Meta Ads pause learning after 48 hours without a sale—here’s how to restart it without losing data or doubling spend.

reel_beats.hook: Meta Ads stop learning if no one converts for 2 days

body.text: Meta’s algorithm stops learning if no one converts for 48 hours, freezing performance.
Check the ‘Learning Phase’ column in Ads Manager—if it says ‘Learning Limited,’ act fast.
Lower your budget by 10% for 24 hours to trigger a restart without losing data.
Wait for one conversion—this restarts the learning phase, then raise your budget back.

reel_beats.send_line: Send this to whoever runs your Meta Ads

body_slides.text: Meta’s algorithm stops learning if no one converts for 48 hours.
This freezes your ad’s performance—it won’t improve until restarted.
Step 1: Check the ‘Learning Phase’ column in Ads Manager.
Step 2: If it says ‘Learning Limited,’ lower your budget by 10% for 24 hours.
Step 3: Wait for one conversion—this restarts the learning phase.
Step 4: Raise your budget back to normal once learning resumes.

carousels.caption: One reply moves your email to Gmail’s Primary tab—here’s how to get that reply in 24 hours and boost open rates. #emailmarketingtips #emaildeliverability #conversiontracking #irishsmallbusiness
carousels.hook: One reply moves your email to Gmail’s Primary tab
carousels.throughline: Gmail moves your email to Primary after one reply—here’s how to trigger that reply in 24 hours and boost open rates.

reel_beats.hook: Gmail moves your email to Primary after one reply

body.text: Gmail’s algorithm checks for replies—one moves your email to Primary, boosting open rates.
Send a short, personal email asking for a quick reply—under 50 words works best.
Use a question in the subject line—‘Quick question?’ gets the fastest replies.
Send it early in the day—morning replies trigger Gmail’s Primary move faster.

reel_beats.send_line: Send this to whoever writes your emails

body_slides.text: Gmail’s algorithm checks for replies—one moves your email to Primary.
Step 1: Send a short, personal email asking for a quick reply.
Step 2: Use a question in the subject line—‘Quick question?’ works best.
Step 3: Keep the email under 50 words—people reply faster to short messages.
Step 4: Send it early in the day—morning replies trigger Gmail’s Primary move.
Step 5: Follow up in 24 hours if no reply—Gmail sees this as engagement.
